description: Security and RBAC scenarios modeled by the Fauxterprise Terraform environment

categories.over-privilege: Users or groups with more permissions than needed
categories.identity-hygiene: Group membership patterns that create unintended access
categories.data-plane: Storage and Key Vault data-plane vs management-plane access models
categories.stale-access: Permissions that should have been revoked
categories.separation-of-duties: Roles that violate least-privilege or SoD principles

scenarios.title: Over-privileged break-glass account
scenarios.description: User 0 has Owner on every resource group in prod_app1. This simulates a break-glass account whose scope was never narrowed after initial setup.
expected_findings: Owner assigned directly to individual user
User has Owner on production resources

scenarios.title: Shadow admin with cross-environment Owner
scenarios.description: User 99 has Owner on all RGs in both prod_app2 AND staging. This models a shadow admin who accumulated privileges across environments without review.
expected_findings: Owner assigned directly to individual user
User has Owner across multiple environments

scenarios.title: User Access Administrator on staging
scenarios.description: User 2 has User Access Administrator on all staging RGs, meaning they can grant others access to staging. This privilege is nearly as dangerous as Owner.
expected_findings: User Access Administrator assigned to individual user

scenarios.title: Stale access on decommissioned subscription
scenarios.description: User 50 retains Reader access on the decommissioned subscription. This simulates forgotten access that should have been revoked when the workload was retired.

scenarios.title: Direct user assignments instead of groups
scenarios.description: Users 10-14 have individual Contributor assignments on prod_app1's app RG. Best practice is to use group-based assignment for auditability and lifecycle management.
expected_findings: Direct user role assignment instead of group-based
Multiple individual assignments on same scope

scenarios.title: Mixed storage access models (RBAC vs key-based)
scenarios.description: Storage accounts alternate between RBAC-based access (shared_access_key_enabled=false) and key-based access (shared_access_key_enabled=true). This inconsistency makes auditing difficult and may mask unauthorized key usage.

details.pattern: Even-indexed subscriptions use RBAC, odd-indexed use key access
details.risk: Key-based storage accounts bypass Azure RBAC, making access invisible to role assignment audits

expected_findings: Inconsistent storage access model across subscriptions

scenarios.title: Mixed Key Vault access models (RBAC vs access-policy)
scenarios.description: Key Vaults alternate between RBAC authorization and classic access-policy mode (opposite pattern from storage). Access-policy vaults are not auditable through role assignments alone.

details.pattern: Odd-indexed subscriptions use RBAC, even-indexed use access-policy
details.risk: Access-policy Key Vaults require separate audit; RBAC-based vaults appear in role assignments

expected_findings: Access-policy vaults not visible in RBAC graph

scenarios.title: Broad platform group with Owner across infrastructure
scenarios.description: The platform-admins group has Owner on all RGs in both connectivity and management subscriptions. While this may be intended for a platform team, the blast radius is significant.
expected_findings: Group with Owner on multiple subscriptions

scenarios.title: Individual storage blob data readers
scenarios.description: Users 20-24 have individual Storage Blob Data Reader assignments on prod_app1's storage account. This grants data-plane read access directly to users rather than through a group.

scenarios.title: Individual Key Vault secrets access
scenarios.description: Users 30-34 have Key Vault Secrets User on the staging vault. This allows them to read, list, and set secrets individually rather than through group-based access.

scenarios.title: Monitoring role sprawl
scenarios.description: Users 60-64 have individual Monitoring Reader on the management subscription. Combined with the it-ops group's Monitoring Contributor, this creates overlapping monitoring access.

scenarios.title: Sandbox with overly broad Contributor
scenarios.description: Users 80-84 have individual Contributor on the sandbox, in addition to the sandbox-users group assignment. The sandbox is intentionally permissive, but individual assignments are still worth flagging.
expected_findings: Individual assignment redundant with group membership

scenarios.title: Network lead with full infrastructure Owner
scenarios.description: User 1 has Owner on all connectivity RGs as an individual assignment. This overlaps with the platform-admins group assignment and should be consolidated.
expected_findings: Individual Owner overlapping with group assignment

scenarios.title: Website Contributor on staging
scenarios.description: Users 70-74 have individual Website Contributor on the staging app RG. This allows them to manage App Service resources directly.

scenarios.title: CAF-lite management group hierarchy
scenarios.description: The management group hierarchy follows a reduced Cloud Adoption Framework pattern with Platform (connectivity, identity, management), Landing Zones (production, staging, development), Sandbox, and Decommissioned. Role inheritance flows down this tree.

scenarios.title: Overlapping auditor and department memberships
scenarios.description: Every 3rd user is added to read-only-auditors in addition to their department group. This creates a cross-cutting group that may accumulate permissions beyond the auditor role.
expected_findings: Users in multiple groups with different privilege levels

scenarios.title: Incomplete ExpressRoute peering to staging
scenarios.description: The hub/spoke network topology includes an ExpressRoute circuit, but the peering to staging is intentionally incomplete. This models a real-world misconfiguration where network connectivity was only partially established.

details.issue: Staging spoke not connected through ExpressRoute gateway

scenarios.title: Service principal proliferation
scenarios.description: Five service principals are created for various automation purposes. Each should be reviewed to ensure they follow least-privilege and have appropriate credential rotation.
